# 2025-2026 영향력 있는 멀티모달/text→image retrieval 논문 — 우리 프로젝트 적용성 리포트

> **검증 기준**: 아래 모든 논문은 Semantic Scholar Graph API(또는 Google Scholar 교차검증)로 인용수 50회 이상이 확인됨. 우리 프로젝트의 3대 발견을 기준으로 적용성을 판정한다 — **(F1)** N=30 gold eval의 통계적 검정력이 진짜 천장이라 어떤 방법도 LoRA+BM25를 유의하게 못 이김, **(F2)** 한국어 char-ngram BM25 lexical fusion이 지배적 레버, **(F3)** training-free 테스트타임 보정(modality-gap / QB-Norm·CSLS / query-bank prior)만 작지만 일관되고 high-power-유의한 이득.
>
> **코드 확인 사실**: 저장소에 `maxsim.py`(ColBERT식 Sum-of-MaxSim), `patch_rerank.py`, `precompute_vision_patches.py`, `hybrid_retrieval.py`(BM25 fusion), `query_expansion_eval.py`가 이미 존재. 즉 **late-interaction·하이브리드·쿼리확장은 이미 우리 SigLIP2 위에서 시도된 레버**다. 이 사실이 여러 판정을 강화한다.

판정 범례: **YES**(돌릴 가치 있음) / **PARTIAL**(아이디어 일부만, 보통 인용·작은 실험) / **NO**(인용만, 실행 부적합).

---

## 테마 1 — VLM-as-Embedder 백본 (디코더 VLM을 임베더로)

우리에게 가장 "현대적 강한 baseline"이 될 수 있는 그룹. 핵심 트레이드오프는 동일하다: cached frozen SigLIP2 + 초경량 text-only LoRA 경제성을 버리고 4~7B 디코더 VLM forward로 대체하느냐. (F1) 때문에 백본 교체가 gold에서 유의하게 이길 가능성은 낮다.

### 1. GME: Improving Universal Multimodal Retrieval by Multimodal LLMs
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2412.16855, arXiv.org (2024) · **140회**
- 아이디어: Qwen2-VL(2B/7B) 기반 범용 멀티모달 임베더. 마지막 토큰 hidden state를 임베딩으로. VLM2Vec 대비 기여는 **fused-modal(이미지+텍스트) 합성 학습 데이터 파이프라인** + UMRB 벤치마크. 오픈 instruct 가중치 배포.
- **우리 적용 판정: PARTIAL→YES(가장 돌릴 만한 백본)**. 이유: 우리가 이미 Qwen2.5-7B를 vLLM로 돌리므로 **학습 0, zero-shot 평가 가능** — 588 갤러리 이미지 한 번 임베딩, 한국어 쿼리 임베딩, cosine 랭크. "현대 강한 baseline" 한 줄로 정당. **비용**: 갤러리 588장 1회 인코딩(저렴) + 쿼리당 7B forward(느리지만 N=30/1706이라 감당). **기대값(F1)**: gold에서 유의하게 더 좋다/나쁘다 둘 다 못 보일 가능성 큼. 단일 dense라 (F2) BM25 레버를 버리므로 **반드시 BM25 fusion과 함께** 돌려야 공정. 한국어 짧은 슬랭 패션 쿼리에서 Qwen2-VL 성능은 미검증 리스크.

### 2. VLM2Vec: Training VLMs for Massive Multimodal Embedding Tasks
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2410.05160, **ICLR 2025** · **176회**
- 아이디어: InfoNCE 대조학습으로 임의의 디코더 VLM(Phi-3.5-V/LLaVA/Qwen2-VL)을 instruction-aware 범용 임베더로. interleaved 이미지+텍스트+instruction의 마지막 토큰 = 고정차원 벡터. MMEB 벤치마크 정립. GME/MM-Embed/mmE5/LamRA의 원형(canonical recipe).
- **우리 적용 판정: NO(프레이밍·baseline 인용만)**. 이유: drop-in이 아님 — frozen SigLIP2를 4~7B 디코더로 교체 + **대조학습 필수(training-free 아님)**. 강점인 instruction-following·interleaved 입력을 우리의 짧은 캐주얼 한국어→상품이미지가 거의 안 씀. (F1) 천장에서 전면 재엔지니어링 비용 대비 이득 기대 0에 가까움. **용도**: "우리는 1주/소규모 체제라 더 싼 dual-encoder+LoRA를 택했다"는 method-section 정당화 인용.

### 3. MM-Embed: Universal Multimodal Retrieval with Multimodal LLMs
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2411.02571, **ICLR 2025** · **131회**
- 아이디어: MLLM(LLaVA식)을 16태스크/10데이터셋에 bi-encoder로 파인튜닝, M-BEIR SOTA + MTEB 텍스트 검색 보존(continual FT). 우리에게 의미 있는 두 아이디어: (a) modality-aware **hard-negative mining**, (b) **off-the-shelf MLLM을 zero-shot reranker로 프롬프팅**(어렵/모호 쿼리에서 가장 도움).
- **우리 적용 판정: PARTIAL→YES(reranker 실험 1건)**. retriever 본체는 무겁고 학습 필요 → 패스. **저비용 이식 가능 아이디어 = zero-shot MLLM reranker**: LoRA+BM25 top-k(30 또는 1706 합성 쿼리)를 로컬 EXAONE-3.5-7.8B/Qwen2.5-7B에 caption+이미지 listwise/pointwise 판정. training-free, 로컬·무API 제약 충족. 논문의 "어려운/모호한 쿼리에서 도움" = 우리 진단(실패는 perception/label artifact)과 일치. **기대값**: gold N=30에선 무유의, **1706 합성 eval에선 high-power-유의 가능** — (F3)의 training-free-보정 승리 패턴과 동형.

## 테마 2 — Prompt-based / 텍스트-only 임베딩 (우리 thesis의 외부 검증)

### 4. E5-V: Universal Embeddings with Multimodal LLMs
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2407.12580 (2024) · **110회**
- 아이디어: MLLM에 "Summarize ... in one word:"로 입력을 한 단어로 압축시키고 그 토큰 표현을 읽어 modality gap을 줄임. 헤드라인: **텍스트 쌍만으로 학습해도 풀 멀티모달 대조학습에 필적/상회, 학습비용 ~95% 절감**. 파인튜닝 없이도 작동.
- **우리 적용 판정: PARTIAL(강한 지지 인용 + 선택적 임베딩 추출)**. 이유: **"텍스트 쌍만 학습으로 충분"이 우리 text-only LoRA 결정의 독립적 외부 검증** — 중심 설계 주장 정당화에 인용 강추. "한 단어로 표현" 프롬프트 + 토큰 읽기는 EXAONE/Qwen으로 LLM-side 텍스트 임베딩을 거의-training-free로 뽑는 길이고 **modality-gap 명시적 해소 프레이밍이 우리 modality-gap 보정과 직접 연결**. 단 이미지측은 여전히 MLLM forward 필요 → cached SigLIP2 대체라 백본 스왑은 비권장. 방어적 용도는 **지지 인용**.

### 5. LamRA: Large Multimodal Model as Your Advanced Retrieval Assistant
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2412.01720, **CVPR 2025** · **92회**
- 아이디어: 하나의 MLLM이 retrieval+rerank 둘 다. Stage1 텍스트-only 대조 사전학습(summarization-prompt 임베딩), Stage2 instruction-tuning 통합 임베더. 별도 **LoRA reranking 모듈**이 pointwise/listwise + hard-sample mining.
- **우리 적용 판정: PARTIAL(reranker 설계 모방 + 인용)**. 두 takeaway: (1) retrieval+rerank-in-one-MLLM 설계가 다시 **로컬 LLM으로 top-k MLLM reranking**을 지지(MM-Embed와 동일 실험), **hard-sample-mining listwise** 프레이밍이 빠른 rerank pass의 모방 대상. (2) 아키텍처는 우리보다 무거움(2-stage 임베더 + 자체 reranker LoRA) → 1주/소규모/천장 모두 부적합. **용도**: "base retriever 위 LoRA reranking" + VLM-as-retriever 지형 인용. 실행 슬라이스는 listwise LLM reranker만.

## 테마 3 — Late-Interaction / 멀티벡터 vs 단일벡터 (우리가 이미 시도한 영역)

### 6. ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with VLMs
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2407.01449, **ICLR 2025** · **146회**
- 아이디어: 문서 페이지를 이미지로 보고 VLM(PaliGemma-3B)이 patch당 128d 멀티벡터(~1024개/페이지) 출력, ColBERT식 **MaxSim late-interaction**으로 미세 매칭. ViDoRe 벤치마크.
- **우리 적용 판정: NO(패러다임 인용, 구현 말 것 — 이미 변형 시도함)**. 이유: 우리는 frozen 588 갤러리에 **단일 pooled SigLIP2 벡터**를 보유. ColPali는 retrieval-tuned patch 토큰 + 그걸 출력하는 생성형 VLM 필요이고 이득이 **patch 벡터 대조 파인튜닝(non-training-free)**에서 나옴. 또 텍스트-in-이미지 문서 대상 — 우리 패션 사진엔 글자 거의 없어 핵심 단어매칭 기제가 안 먹음. **결정적으로 우리는 `maxsim.py`/`patch_rerank.py`로 SigLIP2 patch에 MaxSim을 이미 돌렸고 천장을 못 뚫음** → 백본·patch-LoRA 재학습은 (F1)이 인증 불가. 패러다임 인용만.

### 7. Document Screenshot Embedding (DSE)
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2406.11251, **EMNLP 2024** · **115회**
- 아이디어: ColPali의 단일벡터 반대편 — 문서를 스크린샷으로 렌더, VLM bi-encoder가 **하나의 dense 벡터**로. BM25 대비 top-1 +17pt, 슬라이드 nDCG@10 +15pt.
- **우리 적용 판정: NO(방어적 related-work 인용)**. 우리와 더 정렬(단일 pooled, bi-encoder, MaxSim 없음)되지만 여전히 스크린샷 임베딩용 VLM 대조학습 필요(우리 frozen pooled SigLIP2 아님). **용도**: 단일벡터가 경쟁력 있다는 증거 → 우리 단일벡터 SigLIP2+BM25 설계 정당화, "반드시 멀티벡터여야 한다"는 리뷰어 반박 차단. late-interaction 스킵 정당화 인용.

### 8. VISTA: Visualized Text Embedding for Universal Multi-Modal Retrieval
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2406.04292, **ACL 2024** · **78회**
- 아이디어: frozen 강한 텍스트 인코더(BGE)에 visual token 주입 → 텍스트/이미지/합성 단일벡터. **합성 composed 이미지-텍스트 데이터 생성** 전략, 다단계 학습. R@5 96.3%.
- **우리 적용 판정: NO(related-work 인용)**. late-interaction 각도엔 비껴남(단일벡터). 재사용 가능 아이디어는 **합성 composed-data 생성** — 우리 7k LLM 생성 쿼리와 개념적 평행. 단 인코더 학습 필요 + SigLIP2 버리고 BGE+visual-token 전환. "생성 데이터로 텍스트측 적응"이 정립 레시피란 positioning 인용. 구현 우선순위 낮음.

## 테마 4 — Test-Time Compute / Instruction-Trained Reranking & Retrieval

### 9. Promptriever: Instruction-Trained Retrievers Can Be Prompted Like LMs
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2409.11136, **ICLR 2025** · **56회**
- 아이디어: MS MARCO에서 LLM으로 인스턴스별 자유형식 relevance instruction + hard "instruction negatives"(고립 시 관련이나 instruction으로 무관해지는)를 ~500k 합성, Llama-2-7B bi-encoder 학습 → 쿼리타임 프롬프트로 steerable, phrasing-robust(+14.3 p-MRR FollowIR).
- **우리 적용 판정: PARTIAL(우리가 쓴 바로 그 레시피의 최강 인용)**. 이유: **LLM 생성 user-style 쿼리로 retriever 학습 = 우리가 한 것** → 합성-쿼리 학습이 정당·정립됐다는 강한 방법론 인용. 텍스트-only지만 modality-agnostic, 우리 text-tower LoRA에 깔끔히 전이. 단락 가치 있으나 (F1/1주)로 **구현 비권장**인 두 아이디어: (a) 인스턴스-레벨 instruction, (b) hard instruction-negatives. phrasing-robustness 이득 = "user-query/caption gap이 레버"라는 우리 주장과 공명. **동기부여 인용, 재학습 말 것.**

### 10. Rank1: Test-Time Compute for Reranking in IR
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2502.18418, **COLM 2025** · **66회**
- 아이디어: ~600k DeepSeek-R1 추론 트레이스를 pointwise reranker로 증류, relevance 판정 전 명시적 CoT 출력. 추론 compute↑ → reasoning-IR(BRIGHT)·부정(NevIR)·instruction(mFollowIR) SOTA.
- **우리 적용 판정: NO(F3 프레이밍 인용)**. 이유: 텍스트-only passage IR, ~600k 추론트레이스 SFT + 7B+ reasoning 백본 필요 → 1주/training-free선호/N=30 전부 밖. **재현 금지**. **용도**: test-time-compute reranker 동기부여 + 우리의 싼 training-free 보정(modality-gap, QB-Norm/CSLS, query-bank prior)을 "예산 적정 analogue"로 positioning하는 (F3) 핵심 인용. 실험가치 ~0, 인용가치 높음.

## 테마 5 — Training-Free LLM-Routed Retrieval & Instruction Retrieval

### 11. CIReVL: Vision-by-Language for Training-Free Compositional Image Retrieval
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2310.09291, **ICLR 2024** · **125회**
- 아이디어: 학습 없이 — (1) VLM이 reference 이미지 캡션, (2) frozen LLM이 캡션+수정텍스트를 target 캡션으로 rewrite, (3) frozen CLIP text→image 검색. **"쿼리를 LLM으로 라우팅 후 frozen 대조모델로 검색" 템플릿** 정립.
- **우리 적용 판정: PARTIAL(정신적으론 직접, 형식은 아님 — 문헌 anchor)**. CIR이라 reference 이미지를 가정하는데 우리 순수 텍스트 쿼리엔 없어 파이프라인 비전이. 하지만 **핵심 move(frozen LLM으로 쿼리 rewrite/expand 후 frozen 인코더로 검색)가 우리가 선호하는 training-free, no-backbone-training 레버 그 자체** → 우리 LLM 생성 쿼리뱅크 + query-bank-as-prior를 정립 방향으로 프레이밍하는 가장 깔끔한 인용. 실행가치 낮음(reference 없음, 쿼리별 rewrite는 N=30서 무유의).

### 12. MagicLens: Self-Supervised Image Retrieval with Open-Ended Instructions
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2403.19651, **ICML 2024 (Oral)** · **119회**
- 아이디어: open-ended instruction을 따르는 단일 dual-encoder. 같은 웹페이지 공기 이미지 쌍을 마이닝 + LLM으로 instruction 합성 → **36.7M (query img, instruction, target img)** 트리플릿.
- **우리 적용 판정: NO(instruction-conditioned retrieval 정의 인용)**. 36.7M 웹마이닝 트리플릿(소규모/1주/무대규모 제약 밖), query 이미지 대상 instruction(순수 텍스트 아님), SigLIP2 아님, training-free 레시피 없음. **용도**: positioning 시 "instruction-conditioned retrieval" 정의 + 우리가 대신 싼 text-only LoRA + training-free 보정으로 텍스트측을 정렬한 이유 설명.

## 테마 6 — 백본 자체 (이미 채택했거나 스왑 부적합)

### 13. SigLIP 2 (우리 백본)
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2502.14786 (2025) · **864회**
- 아이디어: sigmoid 대조손실 유지 + LocCa 캡션/디코더, SILC/TIPS self-distillation+masked-prediction, online data curation, multilingual WebLI. 모든 스케일서 SigLIP1 상회.
- **우리 적용 판정: 이미 채택(method anchor)**. **이것이 우리 백본**(siglip2-base-patch16-384). 인용: (a) multilingual WebLI 인코더라 zero-shot 한국어 검색이 비자명하게 됨, (b) 텍스트 타워가 text-only LoRA로 적응하는 레버. **조치 불필요**(vision cached/frozen). 유일한 업그레이드 후보 = 더 큰 변형(L/16, So400m): 가장 싸고 낮은 리스크의 headroom이나 (F1)서 gold 무유의, 갤러리 588 재인코딩(trivial)만 강제. 백본은 training-free, 우리 적응은 아님.

### 14. AIMv2: Multimodal Autoregressive Pre-training of Large Vision Encoders
- 출처/인용: arXiv 2411.14402, **CVPR 2025** · **102회**
- 아이디어: 대조정렬 대신 멀티모달 autoregression — vision 인코더 + causal 디코더가 이미지 패치+텍스트 토큰 자기회귀 복원. 사전학습 후 **텍스트 타워 폐기, 이미지 인코더만 유지**.

survey_summaries: VLM/LMM-as-embedder is the dominant 2024-2025 paradigm for universal multimodal retrieval: take a generative decoder VLM, read its last-token (or 'summarize-in-one-word' token) hidden state as a single instruction-aware embedding, and contrastively fine-tune it into a bi-encoder. VLM2Vec (176 cites, ICLR'25) defined the recipe + MMEB benchmark; GME-Qwen2-VL (140), MM-Embed/NVIDIA (131, ICLR'25), and LamRA (92, CVPR'25) extended it with fused-modal synthetic data, modality-bias hard negatives, and a unified retrieve+rerank MLLM; E5-V (110) showed text-pair-only training suffices and explicitly closes the modality gap; mmE5 (41, ACL'25 Findings) pushed multilingual coverage via self-evaluated MLLM-synthesized data. HONEST FIT FOR OUR PROJECT: as a class these REPLACE our cached frozen SigLIP2 with a 2-7B VLM forward pass per item and require contrastive training, so they break our cheap text-only-LoRA / precomputed-588-gallery economics and are NOT training-free. Given our established N=30 statistical-power ceiling (nothing beats LoRA+BM25 significantly on gold) and the BM25-lexical-fusion lever this family discards, a backbone swap is high-cost, low-expected-payoff for a 1-week capstone. The genuinely actionable, low-cost slices are: (a) GME-Qwen2-VL as a zero-shot open-weights 'modern strong baseline' comparison (no training, fits our Qwen hardware), ideally fused with BM25; (b) a training-free local-LLM (EXAONE/Qwen2.5) listwise/pointwise RERANKER over our LoRA+BM25 top-k, which MM-Embed and LamRA show helps most on hard queries and matches our 'failures are perception/label artifacts' diagnosis and our existing training-free-correction wins (likely high-power-significant on the 1706-query eval, not on N=30); and (c) E5-V and mmE5 as strong supporting CITATIONS for our two core design choices — text-only training (E5-V) and LLM-synthesized multilingual user-style queries with hard negatives + self-eval (mmE5) — with mmE5's hard-negative mining being a cheap, plausibly significant upgrade to our query bank. Net: cite the whole family for framing, run GME as a baseline and an LLM reranker as an experiment; do not re-architect onto a VLM embedder.

Late-interaction / patch-token retrieval (ColBERT-style MaxSim over per-patch VLM embeddings) is a well-established and influential 2024-2025 paradigm: ColPali (ICLR 2025, 146 cites) is the seminal work, with DSE (EMNLP 2024, 115) as the single-vector screenshot counterpoint, VISTA (ACL 2024, 78) as a related universal-embedding adapter line, MetaEmbed (ICLR 2026 Oral, 20) as the newest test-time-scalable answer to multi-vector storage cost, and a SIGIR 2025 reproducibility study (4 cites) that isolates the late-interaction mechanism as the main driver. HONEST APPLICABILITY VERDICT for our project: this angle is largely NOT a fit and should be cited as related-work / limitations rather than implemented. Reasons: (1) The headline win is reading rendered text/tables/charts inside document pages via patch-level word matching — our gallery is fashion product PHOTOS with little embedded text, so the core mechanism mostly doesn't apply. (2) Every method here requires per-patch token embeddings from a generative/contrastively-tuned VLM and TRAINING (LoRA on patch tokens, Meta Tokens, Matryoshka objective); none is a training-free test-time correction on our frozen pooled SigLIP2 cache — adopting any of them is a backbone swap plus re-embedding the 588-item gallery, not a cheap lever. (3) The reproducibility paper's 25-27 pt 'late interaction wins' is confounded: its single-vector baselines (BiPali/BiQwen2) are decoder-VLMs pooled without strong contrastive retrieval pretraining, unlike SigLIP2 which IS a contrastive dual-encoder — so it is not clean evidence that we are leaving large gains on the table. (4) Our binding constraint is N=30 statistical power; we could not certify a multi-vector backbone change as a significant win even if we built it, and ViDoRe v2's multilingual splits exclude Korean, so there is no ready Korean late-interaction benchmark to lean on. Net: keep the single-vector SigLIP2 + Korean char-ngram BM25 + training-free hubness/modality-gap corrections design; use these papers to position our choice (DSE/MetaEmbed support that few/single vectors are competitive) and to pre-empt the obvious reviewer critique in the limitations section.

Surveyed the 2024-2026 contrastive image-text BACKBONE landscape relevant to a Korean text->image fashion-retrieval project built on a cached, frozen siglip2-base-patch16-384 with a text-only LoRA. Authoritative Semantic Scholar citation counts (fetched 2026-05-31 via the Graph API after working around aggressive 429 rate-limiting): SigLIP 2 = 864, Data Filtering Networks = 257, EVA-CLIP-18B = 108, AIMv2 = 102, MetaCLIP 2 = 42; jina-clip-v2 left unverified (API 429, no count invented). Honest applicability bottom line: our project already sits on the single most-cited and most appropriate backbone (SigLIP 2 — multilingual WebLI training is exactly why zero-shot Korean works at all), so this angle is mainly about related-work positioning, not a swap. The only genuinely Korean-capable ALTERNATIVE backbones with open, A6000-friendly weights are MetaCLIP 2 (worldwide multilingual, breaks the curse-of-multilinguality) and jina-clip-v2 (89 langs incl. Korean, Matryoshka embeddings) — worth citing and at most a one-shot zero-shot comparison. The remaining heavyweights are poor fits: AIMv2 keeps only an image encoder (no aligned text tower -> not a drop-in retrieval model and a likely trap), while DFN-CLIP and EVA-CLIP-18B are English-centric and (for 18B) far past single-GPU retraining. The recurring honest caveat is that ALL of these are backbone/scale/data-curation interventions, whereas our established binding constraint is N=30 statistical power plus the caption-vs-user-query distribution gap; none of them is training-free for our cached-vision setup (every swap means re-encoding the 588-item gallery and retraining the LoRA), and given the power ceiling a backbone change is unlikely to produce a significant gold-eval win. DFN's real value to us is conceptual — it motivates curating the training DISTRIBUTION (our LLM-generated user-style query bank) to match the target, the lever we actually pull.

Composed / instruction-conditioned / reasoning image retrieval (2024-2025). The field splits into two waves. Wave 1 (the seminal training-free trio): CIReVL, LinCIR, MagicLens — they made "compose an image + text query without triplet training" tractable by routing the query through an LLM/MLLM or a language-only projection. Wave 2 (2025 "reasoning retrieval"): OSrCIR (CVPR 2025 Highlight) and CoTMR (ICCV 2025) push chain-of-thought / reflective MLLM reasoning over the composed query before retrieval. CRITICAL APPLICABILITY CAVEAT for our project: ALL of these are Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) — they assume a REFERENCE IMAGE + modification text as input. Our task is pure text->image (casual Korean query -> product image), with NO reference image. So none of these frameworks transfer wholesale, and our cached-frozen-vision / 588-gallery / N=30 / training-free-preferred regime makes the full pipelines (BLIP-2 captioning + GPT/LVLM reasoning per query) heavy and statistically un-validatable on our gold eval. The transferable nuggets are: (a) the LLM-as-query-rewriter idea (already adjacent to our 7k LLM-generated query bank + query-bank-as-prior finding), and (b) training-free test-time philosophy. The genuinely citable framing for our report is "instruction/reasoning retrieval is the active 2024-25 direction, but it targets the composed (reference-image) setting; our text-only Korean retrieval deliberately uses the cheaper LLM-side training-free interventions that this line validates in spirit." I also flag QB-Norm (CVPR 2022) as the canonical citation for the training-free hubness correction we already use — not in-angle but load-bearing for our findings #3. Net recommendation: cite CIReVL + MagicLens as the anchor of this direction, OSrCIR/CoTMR as the 2025 reasoning frontier, and be explicit that we do NOT adopt them because the reference-image assumption and per-query LLM cost don't fit a text-only N=30 capstone.

Angle: CLIP compositionality & fine-grained alignment, 2024-2025, with explicit honesty about training-free vs. training-required and applicability to our cached-pooled-SigLIP2 / N=30 / small-Korean-fashion / training-free-preferred setting.

Big picture for our project: This whole literature is a poor fit as a primary lever for us, and the most recent papers in it actually corroborate our established findings rather than offering a method to adopt. Three structural mismatches: (1) Almost every gain in this line requires CONTRASTIVE TRAINING (hard-negative loss on the joint vision+text space), but our LoRA is text-only and our 588-item vision side is frozen/cached — we cannot run image-side or joint hard-negative objectives without re-encoding images and unfreezing, which breaks our pipeline. (2) These methods target COMPOSITIONALITY benchmarks (SugarCrepe-style word-order/attribute-swap probes), which is a different failure mode from ours — our gold-eval failures are label/perception artifacts and an N=30 power ceiling, not relation/attribute-binding errors. (3) The fine-grained region/patch methods (FG-CLIP, ABE-CLIP) require per-patch image tokens and per-token text features, which our pooled-embedding cache does not store.

The single most decision-relevant result for us: SugarCrepe++ and the CLIC/FSC-CLIP/Hard-Positive-Truth papers all independently document that naive hard-negative compositionality fine-tuning REGULARLY DEGRADES image-text RETRIEVAL — exactly the downstream task we care about. That is strong external support for NOT pursuing hard-negative training, and for citing this as a justified scope cut. The only training-free idea worth a paragraph is ABE-CLIP's attribute-token-to-patch alignment, but it needs patch features we do not cache. Net recommendation: cite TripletCLIP/CLoVe as the canonical hard-negative recipe we deliberately skip, cite CLIC + SugarCrepe++ as evidence that compositional FT trades off against retrieval (defensible reason to skip), and keep our BM25-fusion + training-free test-time-correction stack as-is. Expected value of adopting any of these given our N=30 gold ceiling: near zero for a significant gold-eval win.

Fashion/e-commerce multimodal retrieval in 2025-2026 clusters around three threads, with citation counts inherently low because the space is niche/industry. (1) Domain-adapted fashion embedding backbones — the dominant line is Marqo's Generalized Contrastive Learning (GCL, WWW 2025, ~5 SemScholar cites) which produced Marqo-FashionCLIP/FashionSigLIP, the de-facto SOTA fashion T2I encoders (+57% over FashionCLIP2.0). For us this is a candidate frozen-backbone swap (re-cache 588 image embeddings, no training) but it is English-trained with no Korean support, so a zero-shot bake-off against multilingual SigLIP2 is needed before assuming a win. (2) Industry text->product retrieval with LLM/visual augmentation — VL-CLIP (RecSys 2025, Walmart, 13 cites) and Amazon's Multimodal Semantic Retrieval (8 cites) both show that cleaning/structuring the TEXT side with LLMs and fusing product text+image embeddings beats text-only or vanilla CLIP. These validate our central hypothesis (text-side alignment is the top lever) and suggest two cheap, training-free composable experiments for us: LLM-cleaned gallery captions, and image+caption embedding fusion over the 588 gallery — both bounded by our N=30 power ceiling, so expect small high-power-synthetic-significant gains rather than gold-eval wins. (3) New benchmarks / frontier tasks — LookBench (2026, live holistic fashion retrieval, 1 cite) reinforces our multi-eval, anti-single-number stance and our label-artifact finding; FashionMV/ProCIR (2026, multi-view composed image retrieval, cites unverified) marks the research frontier but is composed-image-retrieval (reference image + edit), which does not match our pure text->image task. Net: the most actionable, defensible, training-free-aligned items are VL-CLIP and the Amazon paper (cite to justify text-side + fusion levers); Marqo-FashionSigLIP is the one optional backbone experiment; LookBench supports our evaluation design; ProCIR/FashionMV is recency context only. None overturns our established finding that N=30 power is the binding constraint and BM25 + training-free test-time corrections are the safe levers."}

Angle: reranking and test-time methods for multimodal retrieval (2025), assessed against our cached-SigLIP2 / small Korean fashion / N=30 / training-free-preferred setting. The 2025 literature splits into two camps. (A) MLLM/reasoning rerankers as a heavy test-time stage: Rank1 (COLM 2025, 66 cites) and Rank-K (34 cites) are the canonical text-only 'test-time compute / reasoning rerank' papers but require large reasoning-trace distillation and are not multimodal; MM-Embed (ICLR 2025, 131 cites - most influential here) and UniME-V2 (AAAI 2026, 28 cites) bring this to multimodal, with MM-Embed offering the directly-usable, training-free recipe (prompt an off-the-shelf MLLM as a zero-shot reranker over top-k). Its own finding - MLLM reranking helps complex queries and is roughly neutral on simple short ones - predicts limited gain on our short casual Korean queries. (B) Training-free hubness/calibration on the similarity matrix, which is where our established finding #3 lives: the seminal anchor is QB-Norm (CVPR 2021, 126 cites, the inverted-softmax/CSLS family we already use); the standout NEW work is Dual Bank Sinkhorn Normalization (ACM MM 2025) - a training-free, two-sided (query+gallery bank) Sinkhorn upgrade to QB-Norm that operates directly on frozen embeddings, making it the single highest-value, lowest-cost experiment to add and the best citation to justify our calibration stack (caveat: 0 cites, too recent). NeighborRetr (CVPR 2025, 6 cites) frames hubness as a live problem but solves it during training, so it serves only as rhetorical support for preferring our post-hoc, small-data-friendly fix. Overarching honest read: our finding #1 (N=30 has no statistical power) caps any reportable gold-eval win from any of these; MLLM rerankers are a cheap-to-try-once, low-expected-value 'modernity' paragraph, while Dual Bank Sinkhorn is the one method genuinely worth implementing because it is training-free, matches our cached-embedding + query-bank-prior setup, and should yield a small high-power-eval-significant gain consistent with our other test-time corrections. Citation counts verified numerically via the Semantic Scholar Graph API (per-arXiv-ID citationCount field); QB-Norm context count also from Semantic Scholar.

Six papers across the synthetic-data / distillation / multilingual axis, all with verified Semantic Scholar citation counts (retrieved 2026-05-31; the S2 batch endpoint was the only reliable source as the single-paper endpoint was rate-limited). Influence tier: SigLIP 2 (864) is our exact backbone and the anchor citation; Promptriever (56, ICLR 2025) is the most influential demonstration that LLM-synthesized queries train better, more phrasing-robust retrievers; SWIM-IR (30, NAACL 2024) is the canonical multilingual LLM-synthetic-query pipeline (summarize-then-ask). Borderline-but-on-point: Tamber 'Cross-Encoder Listwise Distillation + Synthetic Data' (2) and its companion (2502.19712) give the cleanest reranker->retriever distillation recipe AND independently confirm that naive contrastive fine-tuning degrades strong encoders -- a useful cited justification for our 'training-free corrections beat more fine-tuning' stance; Syntriever (10, NAACL Findings 2025, Korean team) adds LLM self-verification + synthetic hard negatives; uCLIP (0, AAAI 2025) is the closest structural analogue to our frozen-encoder + tiny-adapter design. HONEST bottom line for our setting: none of these break the N=30 statistical-power ceiling we already hit -- they are almost all text->text passage retrieval and assume training is the lever, whereas our established findings say lexical (Korean char-ngram BM25) fusion and training-free test-time corrections (modality-gap, QB-Norm/CSLS, query-bank prior) are what give high-power-significant gains. Their real value to us is (1) related-work/motivation citations that make our synthetic-Korean-query LoRA and frozen-SigLIP2 design defensible, and (2) two cheap, budget-fitting data tweaks: diversify synthetic query styles (Tamber) and LLM self-verification / summarize-then-ask query generation (Syntriever, SWIM-IR). The heavier proposals (Plackett-Luce preference alignment, instruction-negatives, multimodal reranker distillation) are not worth implementing given the N=30 bar and 1-week budget. Note: Tamber and uCLIP counts are low because they are very recent (May/Nov 2025); flagged as borderline rather than influential.
